page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, utilizing simultaneous multithreading with 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 16 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25% at 2931.08. Multi-core performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 11737.55 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6523.0. Memory bandwidth is stable, measuring 553.22 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 68.67 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. A notable performance tradeoff is observed in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, which registers in the bottom 25% at 36.88 GB/sec.

Given its compute-focused configuration and dedicated CPU allocation, the c2d-highcpu-8 offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads requiring consistent CPU performance without massive memory footprints. It is well-suited for tasks such as software compilation, web serving, and lightweight LLM inference, as demonstrated by its average static web serving throughput of 10.6 GB/sec and 135M model text generation speed of 240.3 tokens/sec.
